feedback.worked_solution:
Here $f(x)=ln⁡(8x)$ is a function of a function. We use the chain rule.First, we express $g(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=ln⁡u,\,u=8x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot 8 \\  & =\frac{1}{8x}\cdot 8 \\  & =\frac{8}{8x} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{8}}{\cancel{8}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
